purpose: Reference-aligned customer browse, PDP, collections, stores, and utility page experiences rendered from backend-owned storefront/category contracts.
ownedConcepts: Product listing title band with customer-safe copy
Client-only Leaflet India map with selected-store zoom
businessRules: Match old SHRESTA reference page structure and wine/gold styling where the route exists in the reference repo.
Do not copy old mock product, category, collection, or store datasets into SHRESTA-WEB-FE.
All product-like cards, categories, collection metadata, prices, image URLs, media variants, and responsive image metadata come from SHRESTA-BE APIs.
Store locator records, filters, service modes, status labels, contact information, and service promises come from GET /api/v1/storefront/stores.

Store locator UI should follow the old reference shape: breadcrumb title band, search/city/state card, selectable store list, Leaflet/OpenStreetMap coverage panel, visit-benefit cards, and appointment CTA.
Store locator markers must be placed from backend latitude/longitude in Leaflet, not list index or random visual positions.

Store locator map rendering should use the direct client component plus inside-effect Leaflet import; do not wrap it in next/dynamic because that can strand the map as a client-rendering bailout placeholder.
A text search that leaves one backend store visible should select it so the map zooms to that store.
Store status and service-mode pills must stay on one line; labels like Same day and Same Day Delivery must not wrap inside the pill.
Customer product listing routes must show 8 products per page across /products, /categories/[slug], and /collections/[slug], with the active page reflected in the page query parameter.
Pagination is applied after the backend-provided product set is filtered and sorted; changing filters or sort returns the customer to page 1.
Listing controls may filter/sort backend-provided page data locally only for UI responsiveness; trusted catalog truth remains backend-owned.
Filter sidebar UI should follow the old reference implementation pattern: icon header, active filter chips, collapsible groups, gold checkbox rows, counts, and clear-all behavior.

Small screens follow the old reference mobile filter pattern: do not render the full expanded filter sidebar inline; show a compact Filters button that opens a right-side drawer with the same backend-derived filter controls.
Filter options and counts must be generated from the SHRESTA-BE storefront/category response, not hardcoded from legacy non-saree reference datasets.
The horizontal price chips are quick preset ranges; the sidebar Price Range section must provide full-width manual min/max rupee inputs instead of duplicating those preset chips.

Horizontal price chips must stay compact and one-line; on phone widths they wrap into a two-column grid so no preset appears clipped, while wider widths may use an internal scroll rail without page-level overflow.
Customer-facing price labels in filters and previews must use the ₹ symbol, and long manual values must remain readable through wide inputs plus formatted range preview text.
Manual min/max price inputs must render empty by default with no visible placeholder text; field meaning comes from the Min price and Max price labels.
Catalog previous/next controls should use the SHRESTA wine/gold premium pager treatment, not plain rectangular buttons.

Visible PDP and filter icons must be semantic and distinct: assurance uses family/badge-specific icons, trust rows use delivery/return/packaging icons, product details use family/type/media icons, price filtering uses the rupee icon, and category rows use family-specific icons.
PDP short and long descriptions must come from backend ProductCard.description and ProductCard.longDescription; frontend fallback copy is only for stale or incomplete responses.
Customer-facing pages must not leak internal architecture wording such as backend, API, metadata, contract, DB, KV, S3, CDN, or implementation terminology.
PDP specifications must translate technical media fields into customer-safe quality/readiness language; never show deliveryMode, version, object keys, or raw media infrastructure values.
The PDP media panel must align to the top of the details grid and self-size to the image so CSS grid stretch does not create blank space under product imagery.
